findings.element: .card[data-id^="seam_"] .cardTitle + .cardNote — the card the seam lands; guard at src/app.js:707
findings.problem: The one card the suite's signature gesture produces is the only card on the board whose note repeats its title verbatim. Driven at 1440x960: peel "Switch on before guests arrive, not when", Send to Tasks, Open in Tasks — the landed card in To do reads title "Switch on before guests arrive, not when" (14px/600 ink) then note "Switch on before guests arrive, not when." (13px/400 at 72% ink), the same sentence twice, differing only by a trailing full stop. The accessible layer says it twice too (aria-label plus the .sr summary). The author wrote the guard against exactly this and documented it ("a note that repeats its own title is noise") — src/app.js:707 compares entry.crossedWords.trim() !== String(entry.task).trim(), and the peeled words carry the sentence's own terminal period while the task-wording field does not, so a single "." defeats it. Every other card on the board earns its two lines ("Confirm marquee sides with the hire company" / "Mara & Finn, Saturday. Terrace plan if dry, marquee if not…").
findings.fix: Normalise both sides before comparing in src/app.js:707. Add `var samish = function (s) { return String(s || "").trim().replace(/[\s.,;:!?]+$/, "").toLowerCase(); };` and use `note: entry.crossedWords && samish(entry.crossedWords) !== samish(entry.task) ? entry.crossedWords : ""`. The card then carries the title alone, which is what the comment already promises.

findings.element: .undo / .undoFor (src/notes.js:1712, UNDO_SECONDS=30 at src/notes.js:260) vs the Tasks strip (src/tasks.js:1330-1340, retired after 6000ms at src/tasks.js:2348) vs .b-undo (src/timeline.js:1270-1300, no timer at all)
findings.problem: One app, one Ctrl Z, three different promises about the way back — and one of them is a broken promise, not a wording nit. Notes writes "Sent to Tasks. Undo [Ctrl Z] for 30 seconds" in a dark 317x46 pill and ticks the number down every second. Tasks writes "<Title> done" — no verb, no full stop, no window — in the same dark pill and silently retires it after 6 seconds, while its announcement says only "Press Ctrl Z to undo." Timeline writes "Menu tasting at The Orchard moved 7 days earlier." in a 1096x64 WHITE bar inline in the sheet at y=514, and it never expires. So a person who learns in Notes that the offer lasts 30 counted seconds ticks a task, looks away, and finds the way back gone at 6 with nothing having said so. Three grammars for one event as well: bare adjective, verb-only, full sentence. Tasks alone runs five grammars internally — "<T> done", "<T> is not done", "<T> added to Review", "<T> moved to Done", "<T> is due Friday".
findings.fix: One window and one sentence shape. Hoist UNDO_SECONDS to a shared constant, replace the 6000 at src/tasks.js:2348/2359/2482 with it, and pick Timeline's behaviour (the offer stands until the next act) or Notes' 30 — but state it identically or not at all; drop the ticking "for N seconds", which is the only moving number in the suite and exists in one product of three. Then set every strip to "<what happened>. Undo [Ctrl Z]": "Confirm marquee sides with the hire company is done.", "Sent to Tasks: Switch on before guests arrive, not when.", "Menu tasting at The Orchard moved 7 days earlier." Same words means the same object too — Timeline's white inline bar should be the dark pill the other two already use.

findings.element: button.filingBtn[data-act="refile"] — labelled N.copy.filingLabel "Filing under" at src/notes.js:1796 (src/fixture.js:615) and hardcoded "What it is about" at src/notes.js:1878; aria-labels at src/notes.js:1741, 1881, 2180; destinationLabel "This task is filed under" at src/fixture.js:632; collides with button.groupBtn[data-act="group-about"] "What it is about" at src/notes.js:2106
findings.problem: One control, four visible names and three spoken grammars — and one of the four names is already the name of a different control on the same screen. The same button (same class, same data-act, same field) is labelled "Filing under" on the writing desk and "What it is about" once a note is lifted onto the reading desk; in the seam the destination picker for the same value is labelled "To". Spoken: "Filing this under Mara & Finn, Saturday 3 October. Change it." / "This note is about The house. Change it." / "This task is filed under: The house. Change it." — three verbs, and only one of the three uses a colon. Meanwhile "What it is about" is the pressed-state toggle in the index head that re-sorts the list, so on notes.notebook those words are a sort mode and one click later the same words are a field label in the margin.
findings.fix: The field is "Filing under" everywhere: replace the hardcoded "What it is about" at src/notes.js:1878 with esc(N.copy.filingLabel), and drop "This task is filed under" (src/fixture.js:632) for the same token. Make the three aria-labels one grammar off that word — "Filing this under <label>. Change it." at src/notes.js:1741, 1881 and 2180. Leave button.groupBtn "What it is about" alone; it is then the only thing in the product with that name.

findings.element: .peelLabel "Tasks has it" at (303,415) (src/fixture.js:649) + .deskFact b "In Tasks as" at (815,276) (src/notes.js:1894) + index head "Already in Tasks" / "4 so far, and every note stayed here" at (231,631) (src/notes.js:2559-2560) + .undo "Sent to Tasks." at (603,818) (src/notes.js:1137)
findings.problem: One press of Send to Tasks, and at 1440x960 the same sentence prints three times inside 373px of vertical span — "Switch on before guests arrive, not when" at 13px/400 under "IN TASKS AS", at 17px/600 under "TASKS HAS IT", and at 15px/400 under "ALREADY IN TASKS". Four labels claim the same fact ("In Tasks as", "Tasks has it", "Already in Tasks", "Sent to Tasks.") and the reassurance is said four times in four wordings: "Your note stays here." (the sheet, before), "Your note is still here, still private, still yours to edit." (the receipt), "…and every note stayed here" (the index head), "Your note stayed here." (the live region). Saying the one thing a person might doubt four times reads anxious, which is the opposite of the register this surface holds everywhere else.
findings.fix: Say it once, in the place a person is looking. Keep the receipt card — it is where the eye is — as "Tasks has it / <the wording> / Your note is still here." Drop the "In Tasks as" .deskFact while the receipt is open (src/notes.js:1894: add `&& !sentTask`); it is the right row once the receipt is closed. Cut the ledger head's "and every note stayed here" (src/fixture.js/src/notes.js:2560) to plain "4 so far" — the sentence above it has just made that promise. Shorten the live region (src/fixture.js:652) to "Sent to Tasks. Your note stayed here." only, and let the undo pill carry the wording: "Sent to Tasks: Switch on before guests arrive, not when."

findings.element: title="Reading a photo happens on another screen. Not here yet." (src/notes.js:1675, 1698, 1800) and title="Notes options are on another screen. Not here yet." (src/notes.js:1633) against the ratified NOT_YET grammar at src/app.js:96-105; ELSEWHERE at src/notes.js:3462-3469
findings.problem: The honest doors were settled in one grammar and Notes' own two closed doors did not get it. src/app.js:96-105 holds five noun phrases naming a destination — "Every project in one list. Not here yet.", "Guides and support. Not here yet." — with the reason recorded in the code (a door's job is to name what is behind it). Notes' photo and options doors instead say the work "happens on another screen", which names a place this product does not have and tells Orla her photo-reading is somewhere else rather than not built. Driven, the same voice reaches the screen reader five more times (src/notes.js:3462-3469). One of those five is broken English: ELSEWHERE.privacy at src/notes.js:3465 concatenates N.copy.privacyLong, which has no terminal period, so pressing "Private to you" announces "Yours until you send something on Your privacy settings are on another screen." — two sentences fused with no punctuation. The same token is concatenated correctly, with the period, at src/notes.js:2656.
findings.fix: Put all of them in the ratified grammar and delete "another screen". src/notes.js:1633 -> "More for this note. Not here yet."; src/notes.js:1675/1698/1800 -> "A photo, read into words. Not here yet." In ELSEWHERE (src/notes.js:3462-3469): more -> "The rest of Signal Studio. Not here yet."; privacy -> `${N.copy.privacyLong}. Your privacy settings. Not here yet.` (note the added full stop); options -> "More for this note. Not here yet."; photo -> "A photo, read into words. Not here yet. Nothing here changes."; retry -> "Sending again. Not here yet. Your note is still here."; destroy -> "Deleting for good. Not here yet. Nothing here is deleted."

biggestWin: The product says the same fact the same way to the eye and to the ear, object by object. Across 425 distinct visible and spoken strings sampled at 1440 and 390 there is not one fixture leak, not one exclamation mark, not one Title-Cased sentence and not one empty region that lies — and the accessible layer is written, not generated: "Milestone, due 1 Aug. Mara & Finn confirmed the tasting… High priority.", "2 days overdue, due 14 Jul.", "Held 2 days, since 14 Jul. Sent Tuesday, no reply yet.", "Edit Menu tasting at The Orchard. Saturday 1 August, in 16 days. Shown to guests.", one shape, every instance. The visible writing that carries the most weight is the best of it: the five lane sentences ("Held by a reply, a delivery, or a decision."), the one true empty state ("Nothing held up."), "Write the thought before it disappears", "Put these back together", "Never mind". Palette matches: three or four indigo-bearing elements per screen, status hue confined to lane state, everything else carried by ink density and fill. What remains between this and 9.5 is not writing talent and not a build — it is that the three products were each edited to a high bar separately and their SHARED vocabulary never was. Every one of my five findings sits on a seam: one field with four names, one undo promise with three windows, one closed-door grammar with two dialects, one receipt said four ways, and one guard in src/app.js defeated by a full stop. All five are copy plus one hoisted constant plus one normalised string comparison — a day's work, no redesign, no decision reopened.
